article_title: Antimicrobial and Anti-inflammatory Effects of a Novel Peptide From the Skin of Frog Microhyla pulchra.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC-labeled brevinin-2MP binds E. coli ATCC 25922 and S. aureus ATCC 25923 in a concentration-dependent flow-cytometry assay.
direct_assay_types: FITC-labeled peptide flow cytometry on bacterial cells

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Effects on Bacterial Cell Membrane; xml:fig=3:FIGURE 3

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Supports cell-surface binding; it does not alone prove killing without the membrane-integrity assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Live/dead staining and SEM support membrane-integrity loss and damaged morphology in E. coli and S. aureus after brevinin-2MP exposure.
source_locators: xml:sec=Membrane Permeability and Morphology Change Observation

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Membrane Permeability and Morphology Change Observation; xml:fig=3:FIGURE 3

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Direct support for membrane-disruptive antibacterial mechanism against the two tested bacteria.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Brevinin-2MP binds RAW 264.7 cells and suppresses LPS-induced NO, MCP-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha production in the tested concentration range.
direct_assay_types: FITC-labeled peptide flow cytometry on RAW 264.7 cells
source_locators: xml:sec=Inhibition of Inflammatory Factor Production Induced by LPS

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Inhibition of Inflammatory Factor Production Induced by LPS; xml:fig=4:FIGURE 4

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Supports anti-inflammatory cellular activity while leaving the direct membrane receptor unidentified.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Western blot data support suppression of LPS-induced MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway activation markers in RAW 264.7 cells.
direct_assay_types: western blot for phosphorylated JNK/ERK/p38 and nuclear p65
source_locators: xml:sec=Inhibition of Inflammatory Response Pathways Activated by LPS

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Inhibition of Inflammatory Response Pathways Activated by LPS; xml:fig=5:FIGURE 5

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Mechanism remains upstream-target unresolved; pathway inhibition is source-supported.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In vivo carrageenan paw data support anti-inflammatory phenotype, including reduced swelling and MPO activity under the tested dosing context.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Anti-inflammatory Effects on Carrageenan-Induced Paw; xml:fig=6:FIGURE 6

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Phenotypic in vivo support; not a direct molecular target assay.

mechanism_summary: Bacterial membrane disruption is directly supported for E. coli and S. aureus; anti-inflammatory activity is supported through RAW 264.7 binding/cytokine/pathway assays and carrageenan paw phenotype, with the upstream host receptor unresolved.
absence_and_boundary_notes: No direct receptor identity is established for RAW 264.7 binding.
